full_story_part1.text: If the boss is eager, things move fast. It's a familiar hope in meetings and business talks. But in talks about bringing Tesla and SpaceX together, that hope may be turned on its head. You think you've stepped on the gas, but the brake lights come on. Concerns are emerging about that kind of turn of events. Musk supported combining the 2 companies, calling it a good idea. However, he says the decision should be left to the special committees of the 2 companies. Don't jump to conclusions. There are still hurdles to clear between he supports it and the merger is decided. According to Reuters, a person familiar with the talks is concerned that Musk's statement of support and the public announcement of the talks could make shareholders look more closely, slowing the negotiations. Support from a big name does not always mean things will suddenly move ahead. Note that this is not a report that talks have already been delayed.

full_story_part1.canonical_text:
“If the boss is eager, things move fast.” It’s a familiar hope in meetings and business talks. But in talks about bringing Tesla and SpaceX together, that hope may be turned on its head. You think you’ve stepped on the gas, but the brake lights come on. Concerns are emerging about that kind of turn of events.

Musk supported combining the two companies, calling it “a good idea.” However, he says the decision should be left to the special committees of the two companies. Don’t jump to conclusions. There are still hurdles to clear between “he supports it” and “the merger is decided.”

According to Reuters, a person familiar with the talks is concerned that Musk’s statement of support and the public announcement of the talks could make shareholders look more closely, slowing the negotiations. Support from a big name does not always mean things will suddenly move ahead. Note that this is not a report that talks have already been delayed.

full_story_part2.text: The louder the support, the more attention it draws. When the star of the show steps into the spotlight, people in the audience watch more closely. Will people think, If Musk supports it, we can relax, or Wait, let's check the details? What matters is not how loud the support is, but the response it gets. To begin with, the special committees of both companies are there to consider the merger. Setting them up does not mean the merger has been approved. To put it another way, they have only reached the stage of setting out chairs for a review meeting. It's too early to pop the party poppers.

full_story_part3.text: Shareholder approval also has to follow certain steps. For example, for certain mergers and other matters, SpaceX's articles of incorporation require approval from holders of Class B shares voting as a separate group, as well as any other required approvals. Musk's support is not a pass that opens every gate. We do not know whether talks will really be delayed this time. So what to watch next is not just Is Musk in favor? but How will others act in response to that support? Will the cheering voices build momentum, or will closer checks lead to cautious driving? A big name's words can fire the starting gun, or give people a reason to stop. Precisely because someone has spoken in favor, we can't take our eyes off the reactions that follow in these merger talks.
